root.label: Casts
root.note: Four named casts with narrow permissions, plus C-style and functional casts that try them in order.

children.label: static_cast
children.note: Conversions the compiler can check from the types alone.

children.label: Direct-init power
children.note: Valid when T t(e); would be, including explicit constructors and conversion functions.

children.label: Reverse conversions
children.note: void* to T*, int or float to enum, base to derived; never removes const.

children.label: Wrong downcast is UB
children.note: If the Base is not inside a Derived, the cast itself is undefined.

children.label: To T&&
children.note: Turns a glvalue into an xvalue; this is what std::move does.

children.label: const_cast
children.note: Adds or removes const and volatile, and changes nothing else.

children.label: Const objects
children.note: Writing to an object created const is undefined, even after a valid const_cast.

children.label: Const paths
children.note: Writing to a non-const object reached through a const pointer is fine.

children.label: as_const idiom
children.note: Implement a non-const member via the const one, then const_cast the result.

children.label: reinterpret_cast
children.note: Reuses an address or bits under another type.

children.label: Pointer and integer
children.note: Round trip through an integer large enough, such as uintptr_t, restores the pointer.

children.label: Pointer to pointer
children.note: Same address; reading through it is limited by the aliasing rules.

children.label: Cannot do
children.note: Cannot remove const, convert arithmetic values or appear in a constant expression.

children.label: dynamic_cast
children.note: Checks the most derived object at run time.

children.label: Needs polymorphism
children.note: Except for upcasts, the source class must have a virtual function.

children.label: Failure
children.note: Pointer form returns null; reference form throws std::bad_cast.

children.label: Cross-cast
children.note: Can reach a sibling base if the most derived object has it publicly and unambiguously.

children.label: void* target
children.note: Returns the address of the most derived object.

children.label: C-style and functional
children.note: (T)e and T(e) try the named casts in a fixed order.

children.label: Order
children.note: const, static, static then const, reinterpret, reinterpret then const.

children.label: Ignores access
children.note: Its static steps may convert to or from an inaccessible base class.

children.label: Incomplete classes
children.note: Unspecified whether static or reinterpret semantics apply, so the address may not adjust.

children.label: T{e} differs
children.note: Braces are list-initialization: implicit conversions only, no narrowing.

children.label: Results and bit_cast
children.note: Value category rules and the C++20 bit copy.

children.label: Value category
children.note: T& gives an lvalue, T&& to an object gives an xvalue, anything else a prvalue.

children.label: cv on prvalues
children.note: Non-class prvalues are never cv-qualified, so static_cast<const int> yields int.

children.label: std::bit_cast (C++20)
children.note: Copies bits into a new object of the same size; trivially copyable types; often constexpr.
